references.text: Tells the story of how Joseph was sold by his brothers, which ultimately led to him ending up in Egypt.
Joseph recognizes his brothers when they come to Egypt to buy grain, but they do not recognize him.
Joseph reveals his identity to his brothers and assures them of his forgiveness.
When Jacob sees the wagons Joseph sent, his spirit is revived—a direct contrast to his unbelief in verse 26.
Joseph speaks to his brothers about God's providence: what they meant for evil, God meant for good to preserve many people alive.
The disciples did not believe the women when they told them about Jesus' resurrection—a parallel to Jacob's unbelief regarding the good news about Joseph.
A clear parallel in the response to the message that 'he is alive' (Joseph vs. Jesus), where doubt meets the impossible.
A parallel concerning God's sovereignty, where the kingdom/power is given to a brother instead of the one who expected it.
